answer: With a Registered domain bound by callback verification with annual re-verification, the account is only as strong as its binding: the registered domain answers a fresh challenge, the callback verification is recorded, and annual re-verification keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so losing the channel means losing the identity, and fakes cannot hide behind throwaway channels. One bridge proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of bindings. Between a ember and a atlas lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to bind.
